exposure: risk of pre-eclampsia (PE) at 35-37 weeks' gestation
risk of delivery with PE: Group A (≥ 1 in 2), Group B (1 in 5 to 1 in 3), Group C (1 in 20 to 1 in 6), Group D (1 in 50 to 1 in 21), Group E (< 1 in 50)
outcome: neonatal unit (NNU) admission for at least 48 hours
cohort: 29,035 women with singleton pregnancies attending a routine hospital visit at 35 + 0 to 36 + 6 weeks' gestation
finding: Pregnant women identified as high risk for pre-eclampsia by the competing-risks model are also at increased risk for other adverse pregnancy outcomes, including gestational hypertension, Cesarean section, stillbirth, SGA, and NNU admission.
mod_finding: Women identified as high risk for pre-eclampsia had a higher risk of Cesarean section delivery.
